promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR)

questions.q: How many inputs does a single NOT gate have?
questions.explain: A NOT gate (inverter) takes a single input and produces its opposite as the output.

questions.q: An AND gate produces an output of 1 only when:
questions.explain: The AND gate outputs 1 exclusively when every input is 1, otherwise it outputs 0.

questions.q: An OR gate produces an output of 1 when:
questions.explain: The OR gate outputs 1 if one or more of its inputs is 1, and 0 only when all inputs are 0.

questions.q: The NAND gate is equivalent to which combination of gates?
options: An AND gate followed by a NOT gate
An OR gate followed by a NOT gate
A NOT gate followed by an OR gate
questions.explain: NAND means NOT-AND, so its output is the inverse of the AND gate's output.

questions.q: A NOR gate produces an output of 1 only when:
questions.explain: NOR is NOT-OR, so it outputs 1 only when every input is 0.

questions.q: An XOR gate produces an output of 1 when:
options: The two inputs are the same
questions.explain: The XOR (exclusive OR) gate outputs 1 only when its inputs have different values.

questions.q: What does a truth table show?
options: The output for every possible combination of inputs
Only the combinations that give an output of 1
The physical layout of a logic circuit
The cost of building each logic gate
questions.explain: A truth table lists all possible input combinations and the resulting output for each.

questions.q: For an AND gate with inputs A = 1 and B = 0, the output is:
questions.explain: An AND gate only outputs 1 when both inputs are 1, so 1 AND 0 gives 0.

questions.q: For a NAND gate with inputs A = 1 and B = 1, the output is:
questions.explain: AND of 1 and 1 is 1, and NAND inverts this to give 0.

questions.q: For a NOR gate with inputs A = 0 and B = 0, the output is:
questions.explain: OR of 0 and 0 is 0, and NOR inverts this to give 1.

questions.q: For an XOR gate with inputs A = 1 and B = 1, the output is:
questions.explain: XOR outputs 1 only when inputs differ; here both inputs are equal, so the output is 0.

questions.q: How many rows of input combinations does a truth table need for a circuit with 3 inputs?
questions.explain: The number of combinations is 2 raised to the number of inputs, so 2 cubed equals 8.

questions.q: How many rows of input combinations does a truth table need for a circuit with 2 inputs?
questions.explain: With 2 inputs there are 2 squared, that is 4, possible input combinations.

questions.q: Which single gate gives an output of 1 unless both of its inputs are 1?
questions.explain: The NAND gate outputs 0 only when both inputs are 1, giving 1 for every other combination.

questions.q: For the expression X = A AND (NOT B), what is X when A = 1 and B = 0?
questions.explain: NOT B gives 1, and 1 AND 1 gives an output of 1.

questions.q: For the expression X = (A AND B) OR C, what is X when A = 1, B = 0 and C = 1?
questions.explain: A AND B gives 0, and 0 OR C (which is 1) gives an output of 1.

questions.q: For the expression X = NOT (A OR B), what is X when A = 0 and B = 0?
questions.explain: A OR B gives 0, and NOT 0 gives an output of 1.

questions.q: A circuit output is given by X = A XOR B. What is X when A = 1 and B = 0?
questions.explain: XOR outputs 1 when the inputs are different, and here 1 and 0 differ.
